jp-20261014-news-1.title: iDeCo Contribution Limits to Expand from December 2026: Key Points of the System Revision and What Employees and Civil Servants Should Check Now

segments.src: iDeCo（個人型確定拠出年金）の掛金の上限額が、2026年12月から見直される予定です。特に会社員や公務員など、公的年金の第2号被保険者の方にとっては、これまでよりも老後資金づくりの選択肢が広がる改正といえます。この記事では、改正のポイントと、年末までに確認しておきたいことを整理します。
segments.tr: The contribution limit for iDeCo (Individual-type Defined Contribution pension) is scheduled to be revised starting in December 2026. For those who are Category 2 insured persons under the public pension system, such as company employees and civil servants, this revision will expand the options for building retirement funds compared to before. This article summarizes the key points of the revision and what you should check before the end of the year.

segments.src: > ※本記事は制度の一般的な解説であり、特定の金融商品の購入や加入をすすめるものではありません。内容は2026年10月時点の情報に基づきます。実際の取り扱いは、勤務先や加入先の金融機関、国民年金基金連合会などの公式情報で必ずご確認ください。
segments.tr: > *Note: This article is a general explanation of the system and does not recommend the purchase of specific financial products or enrollment. The content is based on information as of October 2026. Please be sure to check official information from your employer, your financial institution, or the National Pension Fund Association regarding actual procedures.

segments.src: ## 今回の改正で何が変わるのか
segments.tr: ## What will change with this revision?

segments.src: iDeCoには、加入者の区分ごとに毎月の掛金の上限額が定められています。今回の改正では、会社員・公務員などの第2号被保険者について、上限額の考え方が見直されます。
segments.tr: iDeCo has monthly contribution limits set for each category of participant. With this revision, the way the limit is calculated for Category 2 insured persons, such as company employees and civil servants, will be reviewed.

segments.src: | 加入者の区分 | 現行の上限（月額） | 2026年12月以降（予定） |
segments.tr: | Participant Category | Current Limit (Monthly) | From December 2026 (Planned) |

segments.src: | 会社員（企業年金なし） | 2万3,000円 | 6万2,000円 |
segments.tr: | Company Employee (No corporate pension) | 23,000 yen | 62,000 yen |

segments.src: | 会社員（企業型DCのみ） | 2万円 | 6万2,000円から企業型DCの事業主掛金を引いた額 |
segments.tr: | Company Employee (Corporate DC only) | 20,000 yen | 62,000 yen minus employer contributions to corporate DC |

segments.src: | 会社員（DBのみ・DBと企業型DC併用） | 1万2,000円 | 6万2,000円から他制度の掛金相当額を引いた額 |
segments.tr: | Company Employee (DB only / DB and Corporate DC combined) | 12,000 yen | 62,000 yen minus contribution equivalent of other systems |

segments.src: | 公務員 | 1万2,000円 | 6万2,000円から共済の掛金相当額を引いた額 |
segments.tr: | Civil Servant | 12,000 yen | 62,000 yen minus contribution equivalent of mutual aid association |

segments.src: | 自営業者など（第1号） | 6万8,000円（国民年金基金などと合算） | 変更なし |
segments.tr: | Self-employed, etc. (Category 1) | 68,000 yen (combined with National Pension Fund, etc.) | No change |

segments.src: | 専業主婦（夫）など（第3号） | 2万3,000円 | 変更なし |
segments.tr: | Full-time homemaker, etc. (Category 3) | 23,000 yen | No change |

segments.src: ポイントは、「月6万2,000円」という全体の枠の中で、企業年金などの掛金と合算して管理する形に整理される点です。企業年金に加入している方は、自分の上限がいくらになるのかを、個別に確認する必要があります。
segments.tr: The key point is that it will be organized into a total framework of "62,000 yen per month," managed in combination with contributions to corporate pensions and similar systems. If you are enrolled in a corporate pension, you need to check your individual limit.

segments.src: ## 企業年金との関係を整理する
segments.tr: ## Organizing the relationship with corporate pensions

segments.src: 会社員の方は、勤務先の制度によって上限額が変わります。
segments.tr: For company employees, the limit varies depending on the system at your workplace.

segments.src: - **企業年金がない場合**：上限が大きく広がるため、掛金設定の自由度が高まります。
segments.tr: - **If there is no corporate pension**: The limit expands significantly, increasing the flexibility of contribution settings.

segments.src: - **企業型DC（企業型確定拠出年金）がある場合**：企業が拠出する掛金との合計が全体の枠に収まる範囲で、iDeCoの掛金を設定します。
segments.tr: - **If there is a Corporate DC (Corporate-type Defined Contribution pension)**: You set your iDeCo contribution within the range where the total with employer contributions fits into the overall framework.

segments.src: - **DB（確定給付企業年金）などがある場合**：制度ごとに「他制度掛金相当額」が定められており、その金額によって使える枠が変わります。
segments.tr: - **If there is a DB (Defined Benefit corporate pension), etc.**: A "contribution equivalent amount for other systems" is set for each system, and the available framework changes depending on that amount.

segments.src: 「他制度掛金相当額」は、勤務先の制度設計によって異なります。人事・総務担当者や、企業年金の案内資料で確認するのが確実です。
segments.tr: The "contribution equivalent amount for other systems" depends on your workplace's system design. It is best to check with your HR/General Affairs department or the informational materials for your corporate pension.

segments.src: ## 公務員の方が確認したいこと
segments.tr: ## What civil servants should check

segments.src: 公務員の方も、共済年金の掛金相当額を差し引いた範囲で、iDeCoの掛金を設定できる見込みです。職種や共済組合によって取り扱いが異なる場合があるため、所属する共済組合の案内を確認しましょう。
segments.tr: Civil servants are also expected to be able to set iDeCo contributions within the range after deducting the contribution equivalent amount of their mutual aid pension. Since handling may differ depending on the job type or mutual aid association, please check the guidance from your specific mutual aid association.

segments.src: ## 掛金を増やすと何が変わる？　メリットと注意点
segments.tr: ## What changes if you increase your contributions? Benefits and points to note

segments.src: ### メリット
segments.tr: ### Benefits

segments.src: iDeCoには、次の3つの税制上の特徴があります。
segments.tr: iDeCo has the following three tax-related features:

segments.src: 1. 掛金が全額、所得控除の対象になる（小規模企業共済等掛金控除）
segments.tr: 1. Contributions are fully tax-deductible (Small Enterprise Mutual Relief, etc. premium deduction)

segments.src: 2. 運用で得た利益が非課税で再投資される
segments.tr: 2. Profits earned from investment are reinvested tax-free

segments.src: 3. 受け取る際に、公的年金等控除や退職所得控除が使える
segments.tr: 3. When receiving benefits, you can use the public pension deduction or retirement income deduction

segments.src: 掛金を増やせば、その分、所得税・住民税の負担軽減効果も大きくなります。
segments.tr: If you increase your contributions, the effect of reducing your income tax and resident tax burden will also increase.

segments.src: ### 注意点
segments.tr: ### Points to note

segments.src: - **60歳まで原則引き出せない**：途中で資金が必要になる可能性も考えて、生活費や緊急用の資金とは分けて考えましょう。
segments.tr: - **Cannot be withdrawn until age 60 in principle**: Consider the possibility that you may need funds in the interim, and think of this separately from living expenses or emergency funds.

segments.src: - **運用商品によっては元本割れのリスクがある**：投資信託などで運用する場合、価格は変動します。
segments.tr: - **Risk of principal loss depending on investment products**: When investing in products like investment trusts, prices fluctuate.

segments.src: - **手数料がかかる**：加入時・毎月の口座管理手数料は、金融機関によって異なります。
segments.tr: - **Fees apply**: Account management fees at the time of enrollment and monthly vary depending on the financial institution.

segments.src: - **掛金を無理に増やさない**：家計に余裕がない状態で上限まで拠出すると、生活を圧迫するおそれがあります。
segments.tr: - **Do not force an increase in contributions**: Contributing up to the limit when your household budget is tight may put pressure on your daily life.

segments.src: ## 年末までに確認したい5つのこと
segments.tr: ## 5 things to check before the end of the year

segments.src: 1. **自分の区分と現在の掛金を確認する**：加入者区分と、現在の拠出額を再確認します。
segments.tr: 1. **Check your category and current contributions**: Reconfirm your participant category and current contribution amount.

segments.src: 2. **勤務先の企業年金の内容を確認する**：企業型DCやDBの有無、事業主掛金の額を、会社の資料や担当部署で確かめます。
segments.tr: 2. **Check the details of your workplace's corporate pension**: Verify the presence of Corporate DC or DB, and the amount of employer contributions through company documents or the relevant department.

segments.src: 3. **家計を見直す**：毎月いくらまでなら無理なく積み立てられるかを、収支から考えます。
segments.tr: 3. **Review your household budget**: Consider from your income and expenditures how much you can save monthly without strain.

segments.src: 4. **加入先金融機関の案内を待つ・調べる**：掛金の変更手続きの方法や受付開始時期は、金融機関ごとに異なります。公式サイトで確認しましょう。
segments.tr: 4. **Wait for/research guidance from your financial institution**: The methods for changing contributions and the start dates for acceptance vary by financial institution. Check their official website.

segments.src: 5. **年末調整・確定申告の準備をする**：iDeCoの掛金は、国民年金基金連合会から届く「小規模企業共済等掛金払込証明書」で控除を受けます。書類は大切に保管してください。
segments.tr: 5. **Prepare for year-end tax adjustment/tax return**: You receive deductions for iDeCo contributions using the "Small Enterprise Mutual Relief, etc. Premium Payment Certificate" sent by the National Pension Fund Association. Please keep these documents safe.

segments.src: ## 手続きの流れ（目安）
segments.tr: ## Procedure flow (estimate)

segments.src: すでにiDeCoに加入している方が掛金を変更する場合は、加入先の金融機関に「掛金額変更届」を提出するのが一般的です。会社員の方は、事業主の証明書類が必要になる場合もあります。まだ加入していない方は、金融機関の選択、申込み、審査という流れになり、口座開設には1〜2か月程度かかることがあります。早めの準備が安心です。
segments.tr: For those already enrolled in iDeCo who wish to change their contributions, it is common to submit a "Contribution Amount Change Notification" to their financial institution. Company employees may sometimes need supporting documents from their employer. For those not yet enrolled, the process involves selecting a financial institution, applying, and undergoing screening; opening an account can take about 1 to 2 months. Preparing early provides peace of mind.

segments.src: ## まとめ
segments.tr: ## Summary

segments.src: - 2026年12月から、第2号被保険者のiDeCo拠出上限は、全体の枠（月6万2,000円）の中で企業年金などと合算して管理される見込みです。
segments.tr: - From December 2026, the iDeCo contribution limit for Category 2 insured persons is expected to be managed in combination with corporate pensions, etc., within an overall framework (62,000 yen per month).

segments.src: - 自分の上限額は、勤務先の企業年金の有無や内容によって変わります。
segments.tr: - Your individual limit will change depending on whether your workplace has a corporate pension and its details.

segments.src: - 掛金を増やす際は、節税効果だけでなく、60歳まで引き出せない点や運用リスクも踏まえて、無理のない金額を考えましょう。
segments.tr: - When increasing contributions, consider not only the tax-saving effects but also the fact that funds cannot be withdrawn until age 60 and the investment risks, and think of an amount that is manageable.

segments.src: - 正確な情報は、厚生労働省、国民年金基金連合会、勤務先、加入先金融機関の案内でご確認ください。
segments.tr: - Please check accurate information through guidance from the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, the National Pension Fund Association, your employer, and your financial institution.

segments.src: 制度は変わっても、大切なのは自分の生活設計に合った選択をすることです。この機会に、老後資金の準備について一度立ち止まって考えてみてはいかがでしょうか。
segments.tr: Even if the system changes, what is important is making choices that fit your own life plan. Why not take this opportunity to pause and think about your retirement fund preparations?

jp-20261014-news-3.title: How much is the "Child and Child-rearing Support Contribution" on your payslip? A simple guide to how it's added to medical insurance premiums and how it's used

segments.src: ## はじめに:給与明細に新しい項目が加わった
segments.tr: ## Introduction: A new item has been added to your payslip

segments.src: 2026年度から、公的医療保険料とあわせて「子ども・子育て支援金」の徴収が始まりました。給与明細の健康保険料欄に含まれていたり、別建ての項目として表示されていたりするため、「いったい何の負担なのか」「いくら増えたのか」と気になった方も多いのではないでしょうか。
segments.tr: Starting in fiscal year 2026, the collection of the "Child and Child-rearing Support Contribution" began alongside public medical insurance premiums. Because it may be included in the health insurance premium line on your payslip or displayed as a separate item, many people may be wondering, "What exactly is this charge?" or "How much has it increased?"

segments.src: この記事では、制度の仕組み、加入する保険ごとの負担のイメージ、使い道、そして「実質負担」をめぐる議論を、できるだけ中立的に整理します。
segments.tr: In this article, we will neutrally explain the mechanism of the system, the estimated burden for each type of insurance, how the funds are used, and the ongoing debate regarding the "net burden."

segments.src: ※金額は国が公表した試算にもとづく**目安**です。実際の負担は、加入する保険者や所得、地域などによって異なります。
segments.tr: ※The amounts are **estimates** based on calculations published by the government. The actual burden varies depending on the insurer you are enrolled in, your income, your region, and other factors.

segments.src: ## 子ども・子育て支援金とは
segments.tr: ## What is the Child and Child-rearing Support Contribution?

segments.src: 子ども・子育て支援金は、少子化対策の財源の一部を、社会全体で広く分かち合う目的で設けられた仕組みです。国の「こども未来戦略」で示された「加速化プラン」(年間約3.6兆円規模の施策)を支える財源の一つとして位置づけられています。
segments.tr: The Child and Child-rearing Support Contribution is a mechanism established to share a portion of the funding for measures against the declining birthrate broadly across society. It is positioned as one of the funding sources to support the "Acceleration Plan" (measures on a scale of approximately 3.6 trillion yen annually) outlined in the government's "Children's Future Strategy."

segments.src: ポイントは次のとおりです。
segments.tr: The key points are as follows:

segments.src: - 医療保険の保険料とあわせて**公的医療保険の加入者全員**から集める
segments.tr: - Collected from **all public medical insurance enrollees** alongside medical insurance premiums

segments.src: - 会社員などの被用者保険では、保険料と同じく**労使で折半**する
segments.tr: - For employee insurance (such as for company employees), it is **split between employer and employee**, just like insurance premiums

segments.src: - 2026年度から段階的に始まり、**2028年度にかけて徴収額が増えていく**
segments.tr: - It will be introduced in stages starting in fiscal year 2026, with the **collection amount increasing through fiscal year 2028**

segments.src: 税金ではなく「保険料に上乗せ」する形をとるため、年金受給者や高齢者を含め、医療保険に入っているすべての世代が対象になります。
segments.tr: Because it takes the form of an "add-on to insurance premiums" rather than a tax, all generations enrolled in medical insurance, including pension recipients and the elderly, are subject to it.

segments.src: ## 負担額のイメージ(政府試算)
segments.tr: ## Estimated Burden (Government Projections)

segments.src: 国の試算では、1人あたりの月額平均は、加入する医療保険ごとに次のように示されています(2026年度→2027年度→2028年度)。
segments.tr: According to government projections, the average monthly amount per person for each type of medical insurance is as follows (FY 2026 → FY 2027 → FY 2028).

segments.src: | 加入する保険 | 2026年度 | 2027年度 | 2028年度 |
segments.tr: | Insurer | FY 2026 | FY 2027 | FY 2028 |

segments.src: | 協会けんぽ(被保険者1人あたり) | 約250円 | 約350円 | 約450円 |
segments.tr: | Japan Health Insurance Association (per insured person) | Approx. 250 yen | Approx. 350 yen | Approx. 450 yen |

segments.src: | 健康保険組合(同) | 約300円 | 約400円 | 約550円 |
segments.tr: | Health Insurance Societies (same) | Approx. 300 yen | Approx. 400 yen | Approx. 550 yen |

segments.src: | 共済組合(同) | 約350円 | 約450円 | 約600円 |
segments.tr: | Mutual Aid Associations (same) | Approx. 350 yen | Approx. 450 yen | Approx. 600 yen |

segments.src: | 国民健康保険(1人あたり) | 約250円 | 約300円 | 約400円 |
segments.tr: | National Health Insurance (per person) | Approx. 250 yen | Approx. 300 yen | Approx. 400 yen |

segments.src: | 後期高齢者医療制度(1人あたり) | 約200円 | 約250円 | 約350円 |
segments.tr: | Medical Care System for the Elderly (per person) | Approx. 200 yen | Approx. 250 yen | Approx. 350 yen |

segments.src: これらは平均値です。会社員の場合、**年収が高いほど負担も大きくなる**仕組みで、国の試算では2028年度時点で年収400万円で月額約600円台、年収600万円で約1,000円、年収800万円で約1,350円といった水準が示されています。
segments.tr: These are average values. For company employees, the system is designed so that **the higher the annual income, the greater the burden**. Government projections indicate that by fiscal year 2028, the monthly burden will be in the 600 yen range for an annual income of 4 million yen, approximately 1,000 yen for 6 million yen, and approximately 1,350 yen for 8 million yen.

segments.src: また、国民健康保険には世帯単位の計算や、子どもの均等割に対する軽減措置があります。18歳年度末までの子どもについては、支援金の均等割額が全額軽減される扱いとなっています。
segments.tr: Additionally, National Health Insurance has calculations based on households and reduction measures for the per-capita portion for children. For children up to the end of the fiscal year in which they turn 18, the per-capita contribution amount is fully exempted.

segments.src: ## 給与明細ではどう見える?
segments.tr: ## How does it appear on your payslip?

segments.src: 会社員の場合、支援金は健康保険料の一部として計算され、給与から天引きされます。
segments.tr: For company employees, the contribution is calculated as part of the health insurance premium and deducted from your salary.

segments.src: - 保険者によって、「健康保険料」に含めて表示する場合と、「子ども・子育て支援金」として別に表示する場合があります
segments.tr: - Depending on the insurer, it may be included in the "Health Insurance Premium" display or shown separately as "Child and Child-rearing Support Contribution"

segments.src: - 負担は、標準報酬月額や賞与に一定の率(支援金率)をかけて計算されます
segments.tr: - The burden is calculated by applying a certain rate (contribution rate) to your standard monthly remuneration and bonuses

segments.src: - 事業主も同額を負担するため、従業員本人が見る金額は全体の半分です
segments.tr: - Since the employer also bears the same amount, the amount seen by the employee is half of the total

segments.src: なお、支援金の徴収は2026年4月分の保険料から始まっており、月末締め・翌月払いの給与では、5月支給分あたりから天引きが確認できる場合が多いと考えられます。詳しくは勤務先の給与担当や加入する健保組合の案内で確認するのが確実です。
segments.tr: Note that the collection of the contribution began with the April 2026 insurance premiums, and for salaries closed at the end of the month and paid the following month, it is likely that the deduction can be confirmed starting from the May payment. For details, it is best to check with your workplace's payroll department or the guidance from your health insurance society.

segments.src: ## 財源全体の中での位置づけ
segments.tr: ## Positioning within the overall funding

segments.src: 加速化プランの財源は、支援金だけで賄われるわけではありません。大きく次の3本柱で構成されています。
segments.tr: The funding for the Acceleration Plan is not covered solely by the contribution. It is broadly composed of the following three pillars:

segments.src: 1. **既存予算の最大限の活用**(歳出の見直しなど)
segments.tr: 1. **Maximum utilization of existing budgets** (reviewing expenditures, etc.)

segments.src: 2. **社会保障の歳出改革**による公費・保険料負担の抑制
segments.tr: 2. **Expenditure reform in social security** to curb the burden of public funds and insurance premiums

segments.src: 3. **子ども・子育て支援金**(2028年度に約1兆円規模)
segments.tr: 3. **Child and Child-rearing Support Contribution** (approx. 1 trillion yen scale in FY 2028)

segments.src: 政府は、2028年度の支援金総額を約1兆円と見込んでいます。2026年度は約6,000億円、2027年度は約8,000億円と、段階的に拡大していく計画です。
segments.tr: The government expects the total amount of the contribution in fiscal year 2028 to be approximately 1 trillion yen. The plan is to expand it in stages, to approximately 600 billion yen in fiscal year 2026 and approximately 800 billion yen in fiscal year 2027.

segments.src: ## 主な使い道
segments.tr: ## Main uses

segments.src: 支援金は、子ども・子育て支援特別会計に入り、法律で定められた給付などに充てられます。主な内容は次のとおりです。
segments.tr: The contributions go into a special account for child and child-rearing support and are used for benefits stipulated by law. The main contents are as follows:

segments.src: - **児童手当の拡充**:所得制限の撤廃、高校生年代までの支給延長、第3子以降の増額など
segments.tr: - **Expansion of Child Allowance**: Abolition of income limits, extension of payment until high school age, increased amounts for the third child and beyond, etc.

segments.src: - **妊婦のための支援給付**:妊娠・出産時の経済的支援
segments.tr: - **Support benefits for pregnant women**: Financial support during pregnancy and childbirth

segments.src: - **こども誰でも通園制度**:親の就労にかかわらず、保育所などを利用できる仕組み
segments.tr: - **Universal Childcare System**: A mechanism that allows the use of nursery schools, etc., regardless of the parents' employment status

segments.src: - **出生後休業支援給付・育児時短就業給付**:育休や時短勤務中の収入を補う給付
segments.tr: - **Post-birth leave support benefits and childcare reduced working hours benefits**: Benefits to supplement income during childcare leave or reduced working hours

segments.src: - **国民年金保険料の免除**(自営業・フリーランスの育児期間の配慮)
segments.tr: - **Exemption from National Pension premiums** (consideration for childcare periods for self-employed/freelancers)

segments.src: このように、子育て世帯向けの現金給付だけでなく、働き方や就労を支える給付にも使われる点が特徴です。
segments.tr: As such, it is characterized by being used not only for cash benefits for child-rearing households but also for benefits that support work styles and employment.

segments.src: ## 「実質負担」をめぐる議論
segments.tr: ## The debate over "net burden"

segments.src: 支援金をめぐっては、「実質的な負担はどうなるのか」が大きな論点になっています。
segments.tr: Regarding the contribution, "what will the actual burden be?" has become a major point of contention.

segments.src: **政府の説明**
segments.tr: **Government explanation**

segments.src: 社会保障の歳出改革や賃上げによって、医療・介護などの保険料負担の伸びが抑えられるため、支援金を含めた「実質的な負担は生じない」という考え方が示されています。
segments.tr: The government has presented the idea that because the growth of insurance premium burdens for medical and nursing care, etc., will be curbed through social security expenditure reform and wage increases, "no net burden will arise" including the contribution.

segments.src: **これに対する指摘**
segments.tr: **Points raised against this**

segments.src: - 歳出改革の効果は見えにくく、「実感として負担が増えている」との声がある
segments.tr: - The effects of expenditure reform are difficult to see, and there are voices saying, "I feel like the burden is increasing."

segments.src: - 賃上げが進まない層や中小企業では、労使双方の負担が重く感じられる
segments.tr: - For groups where wage increases are not progressing and for small and medium-sized enterprises, the burden on both labor and management is felt to be heavy

segments.src: - 医療保険の仕組みを使うため、子育て世帯でも負担が生じる(給付との差し引きで見る必要がある)
segments.tr: - Because it uses the medical insurance mechanism, a burden also arises for child-rearing households (it is necessary to look at it in deduction from benefits)

segments.src: - 子どもがいない世帯や高齢世代にとっては、給付を直接受けないため負担感が大きいとの意見もある
segments.tr: - For households without children and the elderly generation, there are opinions that the sense of burden is great because they do not receive the benefits directly

segments.src: 一方で、少子化は年金や医療、介護といった社会保障全体の担い手に関わる課題であり、「社会全体で支える」という趣旨に一定の理解を示す意見もあります。
segments.tr: On the other hand, the declining birthrate is an issue related to the bearers of the entire social security system, such as pensions, medical care, and nursing care, and there are also opinions that show a certain level of understanding for the purpose of "supporting it across society as a whole."

segments.src: ## 私たちが確認しておきたいこと
segments.tr: ## What we should check

segments.src: - **自分の保険者の支援金率**:健保組合や協会けんぽのウェブサイトで公表されています
segments.tr: - **Your insurer's contribution rate**: Published on the websites of health insurance societies and the Japan Health Insurance Association

segments.src: - **給与明細の内訳**:保険料率がどう変わったか、昇給や賞与とあわせて確認しましょう
segments.tr: - **Breakdown of your payslip**: Let's check how the insurance premium rate has changed, along with salary increases and bonuses

segments.src: - **世帯への給付**:子育て世帯の場合は、児童手当などの拡充で受け取れる額も合わせて把握することが大切です
segments.tr: - **Benefits to the household**: In the case of child-rearing households, it is important to also grasp the amount that can be received through the expansion of child allowances, etc.

segments.src: - **今後の推移**:2028年度まで段階的に増える予定なので、家計への影響は年々変わります
segments.tr: - **Future trends**: Since it is scheduled to increase in stages until fiscal year 2028, the impact on household finances will change year by year

segments.src: ## まとめ
segments.tr: ## Summary

segments.src: 子ども・子育て支援金は、月額数百円から千円台の負担が段階的に増えていく仕組みで、児童手当の拡充など子育て支援の財源として使われます。政府は「実質負担は生じない」と説明していますが、その実感には個人差があり、議論は続いています。
segments.tr: The Child and Child-rearing Support Contribution is a mechanism where the burden of several hundred yen to over a thousand yen per month will increase in stages, and it is used as a funding source for child-rearing support such as the expansion of child allowances. The government explains that "no net burden will arise," but there are individual differences in that feeling, and the debate continues.

segments.src: 制度の内容と自分の家計への影響を正しく理解し、公式の情報(こども家庭庁、厚生労働省、加入する保険者の案内など)で最新の情報を確認することが大切です。
segments.tr: It is important to correctly understand the details of the system and its impact on your household finances, and to check the latest information through official sources (Children and Families Agency, Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, guidance from your insurer, etc.).

segments.src: *本記事は2026年10月時点で公表されている情報をもとにした一般的な解説です。金額や制度の詳細は変更される場合があります。個別の状況については、加入する保険者や公的機関にご確認ください。*
segments.tr: *This article is a general explanation based on information published as of October 2026. Details of amounts and systems are subject to change. Please check with your insurer or public institutions regarding your individual situation.*

jp-20261014-intro-logistics-11.title: [Logistics Management #11] Why you get charged 3,000 yen at the door even though it was "free shipping"

segments.src: > 国際物流とは「どこまでが売り手の仕事か」を1つの略語で決め、書類で国境を通す仕事のことです。
segments.tr: > International logistics means deciding, through a single abbreviation, "how far the seller's job goes," and getting goods across borders with paperwork.

segments.src: ## 今日のコンセプト
segments.tr: ## Today's Concept

segments.src: 海外から荷物を1つ運ぶだけでも、実は3つの引き継ぎが起きています。**費用**の引き継ぎ、**リスク**(荷物が壊れたら誰の損か)の引き継ぎ、そして**通関手続き**の引き継ぎです。
segments.tr: Even when you ship just one package from overseas, three handovers actually take place. There is the handover of **costs**, the handover of **risk** (if the goods are damaged, whose loss is it?), and the handover of **customs procedures**.

segments.src: この3つを国ごとの商習慣に任せると必ずもめるので、国際商業会議所(ICC)が共通ルールを作りました。それがインコタームズ(Incoterms)です。最新版は2020年版で、全部で11の規則があります。
segments.tr: If these three are left to each country's trade customs, disputes are almost guaranteed, so the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) created common rules. These are Incoterms. The latest edition is the 2020 version, and there are 11 rules in total.

segments.src: 覚え方はシンプルで、頭文字が売り手の負担の重さを表します。
segments.tr: The way to remember them is simple: the initials indicate how heavy the seller's burden is.

segments.src: | 規則 | 売り手はどこまで? |
segments.tr: | Rule | How far does the seller go? |

segments.src: | EXW | 自社の倉庫に置くだけ。あとは全部買い手 |
segments.tr: | EXW | Just place it in your own warehouse. Everything else is the buyer's |

segments.src: | FOB | 輸出港で本船に積むまで |
segments.tr: | FOB | Up to loading onto the vessel at the export port |

segments.src: | CIF | 積むまで+目的港までの運賃と保険料を支払う |
segments.tr: | CIF | Up to loading, plus paying freight and insurance premium to the destination port |

segments.src: | DAP | 買い手の指定場所まで運ぶ(輸入通関・関税は買い手) |
segments.tr: | DAP | Delivery to the buyer's designated place (import clearance and duties are the buyer's) |

segments.src: | DDP | 輸入通関も関税も払って届ける(売り手が一番重い) |
segments.tr: | DDP | Import clearance and duties paid, then delivered (the seller bears the heaviest load) |

segments.src: ここで一番の落とし穴が **CIF** です。売り手が保険料と運賃を払うので「海の上も売り手の責任」と誤解されがちですが、**リスクの分岐点はFOBと同じで、本船に積み込んだ瞬間**です。つまり航海中に貨物が損傷しても、保険金を請求するのは買い手側になります。「費用の分岐点」と「リスクの分岐点」がズレている——これがインコタームズ最大のポイントです。
segments.tr: The biggest pitfall here is **CIF**. Since the seller pays the insurance and freight, it is often misunderstood as "the seller is responsible even at sea," but **the risk transfer point is the same as FOB: the moment the goods are loaded onto the vessel**. In other words, if cargo is damaged during the voyage, it is the buyer who claims the insurance. The point where costs transfer and the point where risk transfers are misaligned: this is the biggest point of Incoterms.

segments.src: もう1つ大事なのは、**インコタームズが決めないこと**です。所有権がいつ移るか、代金をいつ払うか、契約違反のときどうするかは一切決めていません。それらは売買契約書やL/C(信用状)の仕事です。
segments.tr: Another important point is what **Incoterms does not decide**. When ownership passes, when payment is made, and what happens in case of breach of contract are not decided by Incoterms at all. Those are the work of the sales contract and the L/C (letter of credit).

segments.src: そして貨物が日本に着くと、**通関**が待っています。外国貨物はいったん保税地域に入り、そこから税関へ輸入申告をします(実務上はほぼNACCSという電子システム経由で、通関業者が代行します)。日本の関税の課税価格は原則**CIF価格ベース**。ここに品目ごとのHSコードで決まる関税率がかかり、さらに輸入消費税10%(飲食料品は8%)が乗ります。
segments.tr: And when the goods arrive in Japan, **customs clearance** awaits. Foreign goods first enter a bonded area, and from there an import declaration is filed with customs (in practice, it is almost always done electronically through the NACCS system, with a customs broker acting on your behalf). Japan's dutiable value for customs duty is, in principle, **based on CIF price**. The tariff rate determined by each item's HS code is applied to this, and then 10% import consumption tax (8% for food and beverages) is added on top.

segments.src: 申告に必要な書類は、だいたいこの顔ぶれです。
segments.tr: The documents needed for the declaration are roughly these:

segments.src: - **インボイス** — 何をいくらで売ったかの明細。課税価格の根拠になる
segments.tr: - **Invoice**: An itemized statement of what was sold and for how much. It is the basis of the dutiable value

segments.src: - **パッキングリスト** — 何箱に何が入っているか
segments.tr: - **Packing list**: What is in which boxes

segments.src: - **B/L(船荷証券)またはAWB(航空運送状)** — 運送の証拠。B/Lは貨物の引換証そのもので、原本がないと荷物を受け取れない。AWBは引換証ではない
segments.tr: - **B/L (bill of lading) or AWB (air waybill)**: Proof of transport. The B/L is itself the document of title to the goods, and without the original you cannot receive the cargo. The AWB is not a document of title

segments.src: - **原産地証明書** — EPA/FTAの低い税率を使いたいときに必要
segments.tr: - **Certificate of origin**: Needed when you want to use the lower tariff rates under an EPA/FTA

segments.src: - **他法令の許認可** — 食品なら食品衛生法の届出、電気製品ならPSEなど
segments.tr: - **Permits and licenses under other laws**: For food, a notification under the Food Sanitation Act; for electrical products, PSE, etc.

segments.src: ## 暮らしの中で
segments.tr: ## In Everyday Life

segments.src: アメリカのオンラインショップで、3万円のジャケットを買ったとします。サイトには「Free Shipping」。ところが数日後、配達員に「関税と消費税で◯◯円です」と言われて財布を出す——よくある場面です。
segments.tr: Suppose you buy a 30,000 yen jacket from an American online shop. The site says "Free Shipping." But a few days later, the delivery person says, "That's ◯◯ yen for customs duty and consumption tax," and you reach for your wallet. It's a common scene.

segments.src: なぜか。そのショップは **DAP(輸入通関は買い手)** で売っているからです。送料は無料でも、日本側の税金と通関費用は含まれていません。
segments.tr: Why? Because that shop sells under **DAP (import clearance is the buyer's responsibility)**. Shipping may be free, but the Japanese taxes and clearance costs are not included.

segments.src: 個人使用の輸入には特例があり、課税価格は小売価格の60%で計算されます。
segments.tr: There is a special provision for personal-use imports, under which the dutiable value is calculated as 60% of the retail price.

segments.src: 小売価格           30,000円
segments.tr: 小売価格           30,000円

segments.src: (1万円以下なら原則免税だが、今回は超えるので課税)
segments.tr: (1万円以下なら原則免税だが、今回は超えるので課税)

segments.src: 税金の合計        ≒ 3,700円 + 通関手数料
segments.tr: 税金の合計        ≒ 3,700円 + 通関手数料

segments.src: ※実際は千円未満・百円未満の端数切捨てなどの処理があり、税率も品目で大きく変わります。宅配便では別途200〜1,000円程度の通関手数料がかかるのが一般的です。
segments.tr: ※In practice, there is processing such as rounding down amounts under 1,000 yen or under 100 yen, and tax rates vary greatly by item. For parcel delivery, a separate customs handling fee of roughly 200 to 1,000 yen is generally charged.

segments.src: 一方、日本向けに「関税・消費税込み価格」を表示している海外ECサイトは **DDP** で売っています。売り手が事前に税金を回収し、代行業者を通じて納付しているので、玄関での追加請求は原則ありません。同じ商品でも表示価格がDDPサイトのほうが高く見えるのは、税金が最初から入っているからです。
segments.tr: On the other hand, overseas EC sites that display a "price including customs duty and consumption tax" for Japan are selling under **DDP**. The seller collects the taxes in advance and pays them through a proxy agent, so in principle there is no additional charge at the door. The reason the same product can look more expensive on a DDP site is that the taxes are already included from the start.

segments.src: 企業の輸出入でも構図は同じです。名古屋港からベトナムへ部品を送る中小メーカーが、慣れているという理由でコンテナ貨物にFOBを使ってしまう例は今も多いのですが、FOB・CIFはもともと**在来船で本船の上に積む取引**を想定した海上専用の規則です。コンテナはコンテナヤードで運送人に引き渡した時点で手を離れるため、ICCはFCA(またはCIP)を推奨しています。ヤードで事故が起きたとき「まだ本船に積んでいない=まだ売り手のリスク」という不本意な結論になりかねないからです。
segments.tr: The same structure applies to corporate imports and exports. It is still common for small and medium-sized manufacturers shipping parts from the Port of Nagoya to Vietnam to use FOB for container cargo simply because they are used to it. But FOB and CIF were originally sea-only rules that assume **a transaction where goods are loaded on top of a conventional vessel**. A container is handed over to the carrier at the container yard, so the seller's hands leave the goods at that point, and the ICC recommends FCA (or CIP). This is because an accident at the yard could lead to the unwelcome conclusion that "not yet loaded onto the vessel = still the seller's risk."

segments.src: ## 3行まとめ
segments.tr: ## Three-Line Summary

segments.src: 1. インコタームズは費用・リスク・通関の分担を決める11の共通ルールで、所有権や支払条件は決めない。
segments.tr: 1. Incoterms are 11 common rules that determine the sharing of costs, risk, and customs clearance. They do not determine ownership or payment terms.

segments.src: 2. CIFは売り手が運賃と保険料を払うが、リスクの移転は本船積込時点でFOBと同じ——費用とリスクの分岐点はズレる。
segments.tr: 2. Under CIF, the seller pays freight and insurance, but risk transfers at the moment of loading onto the vessel, the same as FOB. The point where costs and risk transfer are misaligned.

segments.src: 3. 通関では関税(日本はCIF価格ベース)と輸入消費税がかかり、インボイス・パッキングリスト・B/L(AWB)・必要に応じて原産地証明書が要る。
segments.tr: 3. Customs clearance involves customs duty (based on CIF price in Japan) and import consumption tax, and requires an invoice, packing list, B/L (or AWB), and a certificate of origin if needed.

segments.src: ## ✅ セルフクイズ
segments.tr: ## ✅ Self-Quiz

segments.src: **Q1.** FOBとCIFの違いについて、正しい説明はどれ?
segments.tr: **Q1.** Which is the correct explanation of the difference between FOB and CIF?

segments.src: - (A) CIFでは航海中のリスクも売り手が負う
segments.tr: - (A) Under CIF, the seller also bears the risk during the voyage

segments.src: - (B) CIFは売り手が運賃・保険料を負担するが、リスクの分岐点はFOBと同じ
segments.tr: - (B) Under CIF, the seller bears freight and insurance, but the risk transfer point is the same as FOB

segments.src: - (C) CIFは航空輸送専用の規則である
segments.tr: - (C) CIF is a rule exclusively for air transport

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) インコタームズは、貨物の所有権がいつ買い手に移るかを定めている。
segments.tr: **Q2.** (T/F) Incoterms define when ownership of the goods passes to the buyer.

segments.src: **Q3.** 日本の商業輸入で、関税の課税価格の原則的な基礎になるのは?
segments.tr: **Q3.** In Japanese commercial imports, what is the basic principle for the base of the dutiable value for customs duty?

segments.src: - (A) FOB価格
segments.tr: - (A) FOB price

segments.src: - (B) CIF価格
segments.tr: - (B) CIF price

segments.src: - (C) 国内の小売価格
segments.tr: - (C) Domestic retail price

segments.src: ## 📚 今日の用語
segments.tr: ## 📚 Today's Terms

segments.src: - **インコタームズ(Incoterms 2020)** — 売り手と買い手の費用・リスク・通関の分担を定めたICCの国際規則(全11規則)。
segments.tr: - **Incoterms (Incoterms 2020)**: The ICC's international rules that define the sharing of costs, risk, and customs clearance between seller and buyer (11 rules in total).

segments.src: - **FOB / CIF** — いずれも海上・内陸水路専用の規則。リスク移転はどちらも本船積込時点で、CIFは売り手が運賃と保険料も払う点だけが違う。
segments.tr: - **FOB / CIF**: Both are rules exclusively for sea and inland waterway transport. Risk transfers at the moment of loading onto the vessel in both; the only difference is that under CIF the seller also pays freight and insurance.

segments.src: - **DAP / DDP** — 買い手の指定場所まで届ける規則。輸入通関と関税を売り手が負担するのがDDP、買い手が負担するのがDAP。
segments.tr: - **DAP / DDP**: Rules for delivering to the buyer's designated place. Under DDP the seller bears import clearance and duties; under DAP the buyer bears them.

segments.src: - **通関** — 貨物を税関に申告し、輸入(輸出)の許可を受ける手続き。日本ではNACCS経由で通関業者が代行するのが一般的。
segments.tr: - **Customs clearance**: The procedure of declaring goods to customs and receiving permission for import (or export). In Japan, it is common for a customs broker to handle this via NACCS.

segments.src: - **B/L(船荷証券)** — 海上運送で発行される貨物の引換証。原本と引き換えでなければ貨物を受け取れない点が、引換証ではないAWB(航空運送状)と大きく異なる。
segments.tr: - **B/L (bill of lading)**: A document of title for goods issued in sea transport. It differs greatly from the AWB (air waybill), which is not a document of title, in that the goods cannot be received without surrendering the original.

segments.src: - **HSコード** — 世界共通の品目分類番号。これで関税率とEPAの適用可否が決まる。
segments.tr: - **HS code**: A globally common product classification number. It determines tariff rates and whether an EPA applies.

segments.src: *正解: Q1 — (B)。CIFの「I」は保険(Insurance)ですが、それは売り手が保険を手配・支払う義務であって、リスクを負い続けるという意味ではありません。保険金を請求する立場になるのは買い手です。
segments.tr: *Answer: Q1 — (B). The "I" in CIF stands for Insurance, but that means the seller is obligated to arrange and pay for insurance, not that the seller keeps bearing the risk. It is the buyer who becomes entitled to claim the insurance proceeds.

segments.src: / Q2 — ×。インコタームズが決めるのは費用・リスク・通関手続きの分担だけで、所有権の移転時期や支払条件は売買契約書で別に定めます。
segments.tr: / Q2 — ×. Incoterms only determine the sharing of costs, risk, and customs procedures. The timing of the transfer of ownership and the payment terms are set separately in the sales contract.

segments.src: / Q3 — (B)。日本の関税評価は原則CIF価格(貨物代金+日本の輸入港までの運賃・保険料)が基礎です。記事中の「小売価格の60%」は個人使用の輸入に適用される特例で、商業輸入には使えません。*
segments.tr: / Q3 — (B). Japan's customs valuation is, in principle, based on CIF price (the goods price plus freight and insurance to the Japanese import port). The "60% of retail price" in the article is a special provision that applies to personal-use imports and cannot be used for commercial imports.*

jp-20261014-news-2.title: Rapidus's 2nm Semiconductors: The Current Situation Before Mass Production Begins—Analyzing the Scale of Public Support and the Odds of Success for 'Domestic Advanced Semiconductors'

segments.src: 北海道・千歳市で建設と試作が進む次世代半導体の国産化プロジェクト、ラピダス（Rapidus）。2027年ごろの量産開始を目標に掲げる同社は、日本の半導体産業の再生を象徴する存在として注目されてきました。本稿では、これまでの公的支援の規模、顧客獲得や人材確保といった課題、そして量産に向けたスケジュールを、できるだけ冷静に整理します。
segments.tr: Rapidus, a domestic production project for next-generation semiconductors, is currently under construction and prototyping in Chitose City, Hokkaido. Aiming to begin mass production around 2027, the company has attracted attention as a symbol of the revitalization of Japan's semiconductor industry. This article calmly analyzes the scale of public support to date, challenges such as customer acquisition and securing human resources, and the schedule toward mass production.

segments.src: > 本稿は公表資料や報道で伝えられてきた内容をもとにした解説です。金額や計画は更新されることがあるため、最新の情報は経済産業省や同社の発表をご確認ください。
segments.tr: > This article is a commentary based on information conveyed in public materials and reports. Because amounts and plans are subject to update, please check the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry or the company's announcements for the latest information.

segments.src: ## ラピダスとは何をめざす会社か
segments.tr: ## What Kind of Company is Rapidus Aiming to Be?

segments.src: ラピダスは2022年に設立された半導体の製造企業です。回路線幅2ナノメートル（nm）世代という最先端のロジック半導体を、国内で量産することをめざしています。
segments.tr: Rapidus is a semiconductor manufacturing company established in 2022. It aims to domestically mass-produce cutting-edge logic semiconductors of the 2-nanometer (nm) circuit line width generation.

segments.src: 特徴は、次の点にあります。
segments.tr: Its characteristics lie in the following points:

segments.src: - **製造に特化する**：自社で製品を設計して売るのではなく、顧客の設計した半導体を受託製造する「ファウンドリー」型のモデルです。
segments.tr: - **Specializing in manufacturing**: Rather than designing and selling its own products, it uses a "foundry" model to contract manufacture semiconductors designed by customers.

segments.src: - **短納期を強みに据える**：ウエハーを1枚ずつ処理する枚葉方式などを活用し、設計から製造までの期間を短くする構想を打ち出しています。
segments.tr: - **Setting short delivery times as a strength**: By utilizing a single-wafer processing method that handles wafers one by one, it has put forward a concept to shorten the period from design to manufacturing.

segments.src: - **海外との連携**：技術面では米IBMやベルギーの研究機関imecなどと協力関係を築いてきました。
segments.tr: - **Collaboration with overseas entities**: On the technical side, it has built cooperative relationships with U.S.-based IBM and Belgium's research institution imec, among others.

segments.src: 国内の最先端ロジック半導体の製造は、40nm前後の世代で止まっていた時期が長く、先端品の多くを海外の工場に頼っているのが現状です。経済安全保障の観点から、国内に先端工場を持つ意義が語られてきた背景があります。
segments.tr: The domestic manufacturing of cutting-edge logic semiconductors had long stopped at the 40nm or so generation, and the current reality is that many advanced products rely on overseas factories. From the perspective of economic security, the significance of having advanced factories domestically has been discussed.

segments.src: ## これまでの公的支援の規模
segments.tr: ## The Scale of Public Support to Date

segments.src: ラピダスは、民間の出資だけでは賄えない巨額の投資が必要な事業です。政府は段階的に支援を積み増してきました。
segments.tr: Rapidus is a business that requires enormous investment that cannot be covered solely by private investment. The government has gradually increased its support.

segments.src: - 2022年度以降、研究開発の委託費などとして国の支援が決まり、その後も年度ごとに追加が行われてきました。
segments.tr: - Starting from fiscal 2022, government support was decided for research and development consignment costs and the like, and additions have been made every fiscal year since.

segments.src: - 報道などによれば、これまでに決定した支援の累計は1兆7千億円を超える規模とされています。
segments.tr: - According to reports and other sources, the cumulative total of support decided so far is said to be on the scale of over 1.7 trillion yen.

segments.src: - 2025年には、政府が出資できるよう法制度が整えられ、補助金に加えて資本面でも関与する枠組みが加わりました。
segments.tr: - In 2025, legal systems were established to enable government investment, adding a framework to participate in terms of capital in addition to subsidies.

segments.src: - 量産に向けた総投資額は、5兆円規模に上るとの見方が示されてきました。
segments.tr: - Views have been presented that the total investment amount toward mass production will reach the scale of 5 trillion yen.

segments.src: つまり、公的支援は今後も続く可能性が高く、民間からの出資や金融機関による融資をどこまで集められるかが、事業の持続性を左右します。
segments.tr: In other words, public support is likely to continue in the future, and how much private investment and loans from financial institutions can be gathered will determine the sustainability of the business.

segments.src: ### 「巨額支援」をどう見るか
segments.tr: ### How to View "Enormous Support"

segments.src: 支援の是非については、さまざまな意見があります。
segments.tr: There are various opinions regarding the pros and cons of support.

segments.src: - **肯定的な見方**：先端半導体の供給網を国内に持つことは、産業と安全保障の両面で意味がある。各国が補助金を出して誘致競争をしている以上、日本も一定の投資は避けられない。
segments.tr: - **Positive perspective**: Having a supply chain for advanced semiconductors domestically is meaningful in both industrial and security terms. Since various countries are providing subsidies and competing to attract them, a certain level of investment is unavoidable for Japan as well.

segments.src: - **慎重な見方**：成功が保証されない事業に巨額の税金を投じることへの懸念がある。支援の成果を測る基準や、情報の公開のあり方が問われる。
segments.tr: - **Cautious perspective**: There are concerns about pouring huge amounts of tax money into a business whose success is not guaranteed. Standards for measuring the results of support and the manner of information disclosure are being questioned.

segments.src: どちらの立場でも共通するのは、「投資額に見合う成果をどう確認するか」という透明性の確保が重要だという点です。
segments.tr: Common to both stances is the point that ensuring transparency—such as how to confirm results commensurate with the investment amount—is important.

segments.src: ## 勝算を左右する三つの課題
segments.tr: ## Three Challenges That Will Determine the Odds of Success

segments.src: ### 1. 顧客の獲得
segments.tr: ### 1. Customer Acquisition

segments.src: ファウンドリーにとって最大の課題は、安定して注文をくれる顧客を確保することです。先端プロセスは開発費も製造設備も高額で、一定量の受注がなければ採算が合いません。
segments.tr: The biggest challenge for a foundry is securing customers who will place orders stably. Advanced processes have expensive development costs and manufacturing equipment, and without a certain amount of orders, it will not be profitable.

segments.src: - 世界の先端ファウンドリー市場では、台湾TSMCが圧倒的な存在感を持っています。
segments.tr: - In the global advanced foundry market, Taiwan's TSMC holds an overwhelming presence.

segments.src: - 韓国のサムスン電子や米インテルも先端分野への投資を続けており、競争は激しい状況です。
segments.tr: - South Korea's Samsung Electronics and the U.S. Intel are also continuing investments in the advanced field, making the competition fierce.

segments.src: - ラピダスは設計企業との協議や、設計支援の環境（PDK）の提供を進めるとしていますが、量産規模の顧客が確定していくかが焦点です。
segments.tr: - Rapidus states that it is advancing discussions with design companies and providing a design support environment (PDK), but whether mass-production-scale customers will be confirmed is the focal point.

segments.src: 後発の企業が先行勢に挑む以上、「価格」や「納期」だけでなく、歩留まり（良品率）や品質の実績をどう積み上げるかが問われます。
segments.tr: As a latecomer challenges the frontrunners, it is questioned how they will build up track records not only in "price" and "delivery time" but also in yield (good product rate) and quality.

segments.src: ### 2. 人材の確保
segments.tr: ### 2. Securing Human Resources

segments.src: 最先端の製造ラインを動かすには、プロセス技術者、設備のエンジニア、設計支援の担当者など、多様な専門人材が必要です。
segments.tr: Operating a cutting-edge manufacturing line requires diverse specialized personnel, such as process engineers, equipment engineers, and design support personnel.

segments.src: - 国内では先端ロジックの量産経験を持つ人材が限られており、海外からの招へいや、大学・高専との連携による育成が進められています。
segments.tr: - Domestically, human resources with experience in mass-producing advanced logic are limited, and recruitment from overseas and development through collaboration with universities and technical colleges are progressing.

segments.src: - 千歳周辺では、人材の受け入れや住環境、地域のインフラ整備も課題として語られています。
segments.tr: - Around Chitose, accepting human resources, the living environment, and the development of regional infrastructure are also discussed as challenges.

segments.src: 技術の習得と人材の定着は時間を要するため、量産時期の目標に対して余裕があるとは言い切れません。
segments.tr: Because acquiring technology and retaining human resources take time, it cannot be said that there is leeway regarding the target timing for mass production.

segments.src: ### 3. 技術の完成度と資金計画
segments.tr: ### 3. Technological Perfection and Financial Planning

segments.src: 2025年には2nm世代のトランジスタの試作に成功したと発表され、技術面で一つの節目を迎えました。ただし、試作ができることと、安定的に量産できることの間には大きな差があります。
segments.tr: In 2025, it was announced that the prototyping of 2nm generation transistors succeeded, marking a milestone in terms of technology. However, there is a big difference between being able to prototype and being able to mass-produce stably.

segments.src: - 歩留まりを実用水準に引き上げるには、長い試行錯誤が必要になるのが一般的です。
segments.tr: - Raising the yield to a practical level generally requires a long process of trial and error.

segments.src: - 装置の導入や稼働の遅れ、為替や資材価格の変動は、費用の増加につながりえます。
segments.tr: - Delays in the introduction or operation of equipment, and fluctuations in exchange rates and material prices, can lead to increased costs.

segments.src: - 次の世代（1.4nmなど）の工場構想も語られており、追加の資金調達が続くことになります。
segments.tr: - Factory concepts for the next generation (such as 1.4nm) are also being discussed, which means additional fundraising will continue.

segments.src: ## 量産に向けたスケジュールの見方
segments.tr: ## How to View the Schedule Toward Mass Production

segments.src: 公表されている計画の大まかな流れは、次のとおりです。
segments.tr: The general flow of the announced plans is as follows:

segments.src: | 時期 | 内容 |
segments.tr: | Timing | Content |

segments.src: | 2023年 | 千歳市で工場（IIM-1）の建設を開始 |
segments.tr: | 2023 | Started construction of the factory (IIM-1) in Chitose City |

segments.src: | 2025年 | パイロットラインの稼働開始、2nm試作の発表 |
segments.tr: | 2025 | Pilot line operation started, announcement of 2nm prototyping |

segments.src: | 2026年 | 顧客向けの設計環境（PDK）の提供と、顧客との協議を進める段階 |
segments.tr: | 2026 | Stage of providing design environment (PDK) for customers and advancing discussions with customers |

segments.src: | 2027年ごろ | 量産開始を目標 |
segments.tr: | Around 2027 | Aiming to start mass production |

segments.src: スケジュールは目標であり、半導体の新工場では計画の見直しが起こることも珍しくありません。今後は、顧客との契約が具体化するか、試作品の評価結果がどう公表されるか、追加の資金調達が円滑に進むかといった点が、進捗を測る目安になります。
segments.tr: Schedules are targets, and it is not uncommon for plans to be revised at new semiconductor factories. Moving forward, points such as whether contracts with customers materialize, how prototype evaluation results are announced, and whether additional fundraising proceeds smoothly will serve as benchmarks to measure progress.

segments.src: ## 「国産先端半導体」の勝算をどう考えるか
segments.tr: ## How to Think About the Odds of Success for "Domestic Advanced Semiconductors"

segments.src: 勝算を一言で示すことは難しいものの、整理すれば次のようになります。
segments.tr: Although it is difficult to express the odds of success in a single word, organizing them yields the following:

segments.src: - **追い風**：各国で供給網の分散が意識されており、地政学的な理由から、複数拠点での生産を望む顧客がいる。
segments.tr: - **Tailwinds**: The diversification of supply chains is being recognized in various countries, and for geopolitical reasons, there are customers who desire production at multiple bases.

segments.src: - **向かい風**：先行企業との技術・コスト面の差、顧客の確保、人材と資金の継続的な調達という、いずれも簡単ではない課題が重なる。
segments.tr: - **Headwinds**: Difficult challenges overlap, including the technological and cost gap with leading companies, securing customers, and the continuous procurement of human resources and funds, none of which are easy.

segments.src: - **鍵となるもの**：早期に実績のある顧客を獲得し、量産品質を示せるかどうか。
segments.tr: - **Key elements**: Whether customers with track records can be acquired early, and whether mass-production quality can be demonstrated.

segments.src: 「国産」であること自体が価値になる場面はあっても、最終的には、性能・価格・納期・信頼性という通常の競争条件で選ばれる必要があります。
segments.tr: Even if there are situations where being "domestic" itself becomes a value, ultimately, it is necessary to be chosen under normal competitive conditions of performance, price, delivery time, and reliability.

segments.src: ## まとめ
segments.tr: ## Conclusion

segments.src: ラピダスのプロジェクトは、日本の半導体産業にとって大きな挑戦です。公的支援はすでに大規模であり、今後も資金面の課題は続きます。顧客獲得、人材確保、量産品質の三つをどこまで具体的な成果として示せるかが、今後数年間の注目点といえるでしょう。
segments.tr: Rapidus's project is a major challenge for Japan's semiconductor industry. Public support is already large-scale, and financial challenges will continue. Whether customer acquisition, human resource securing, and mass-production quality can be demonstrated as concrete results to what extent will likely be the points of attention for the next few years.

segments.src: 私たちにできるのは、期待や不安だけで判断せず、公表される数字やスケジュールの変化を丁寧に追うことです。続報が出た際は、一次情報である政府や企業の発表に当たり、冷静に確認していくことが大切です。
segments.tr: What we can do is not judge solely by expectations or anxieties, but carefully track changes in announced figures and schedules. When follow-up reports are released, it is important to consult the primary information—announcements by the government and companies—and check them calmly.
